stitchTypes.value: 18 stitch variations per Bernina's flyer: 1 four-thread overlock; 8 three-thread (overlock wide and narrow, super-stretch, flatlock wide and narrow, narrow seam, rolled hem, picot); 9 two-thread (overlock wide and narrow, flatlock wide and narrow, rolled hem, wrapped overlock wide and narrow, blanket stitch wide and narrow). No coverstitch or chainstitch

differentialFeed.value: Adjustable while sewing, range 0.7 to 2 (manual p. 101); gather at 1.5 to 2, prevent puckering at 0.7 to 1

needleSystem.value: ELx705 CF, sizes 70 to 90 (10 to 14); the manual also permits 130/705 H needles 'if required'

presserFootLift.value: 2-step lifter with front-foot lift (front foot lifts a further 3 to 4 mm); knee lifter (Free Hand System); swing-out foot with auto swing back; 6-step presser foot pressure. No total lift height published

threadTrimmer.value: Manual thread-chain cutter on the outside of the machine (manual p. 40); no automatic trimmer listed

feedSystem.value: Differential feed; Micro Thread Control (mtc) adjustable while sewing; automatic needle stop up

motor.value: DC motor; energy consumption 140 W (not a rated motor output); input 100 to 240 V

dimensionsIn.value: 16.9 x 11.0 x 13.8 (43 x 28 x 35 cm) without thread stand; 22.4 x 13.8 x 13.8 (57 x 35 x 35 cm) with slide-on table and cut-offs bin

includedFeet.value: Flyer lists: standard overlock foot #L10 with tape guide, slide-on extension table, accessories box, cut-offs bin, right seam guide, tweezers, manual needle threader, ELX705 CF needle set, brush, screwdriver, dust cover. The standard accessories page lists only dust cover, power cable, foot control, knife cover insert, needle set, spool nets and discs, T10 screwdriver

warrantyUs.value: Bernina's general US warranty, not model-specific: 20 yr mechanical parts, 5 yr printed circuit boards, 2 yr electrical parts; parts only, labor and shipping not covered; original purchaser, private use

threadingSystem.value: One-Step Air Threader for both loopers via foot control; built-in needle threader

stitchLengthMm.value: 0.8 to 4.5, adjustable while sewing; 0.8 to 1.5 fine adjustment for rolled hem

"Extremely fast, precise and quiet" (Bernina product page; no decibel figure is published)
"Designed and engineered in Switzerland" (Bernina product page)
More room to the right of the needle and more work space height than any other Bernina serger (Bernina product page)

conflicts: Dimensions: a dealer listing gives 18 x 13 x 16 in, while Bernina's manual gives 43 x 28 x 35 cm (16.9 x 11.0 x 13.8 in) without the thread stand; we use Bernina's.

Stitch split: our earlier count was 1 four-thread, 8 three-thread and 8 two-thread, while Bernina's flyer table lists 1/8/9 (it adds wrapped overlock and blanket stitch to the two-thread group); the total of 18 agrees.

Included accessories: Bernina's flyer lists the overlock foot, extension table and accessories box, while the standard accessories page omits them; no Bernina L 850 document says the accessories box is optional.
Needles: a dealer listing names only ELx705 sizes 70 to 90, while Bernina's manual also permits 130/705 H needles if required.
Space right of the needle: Bernina quotes 5 5/8 in (143 mm) as 'space to the right of the needle' and never as needle-to-arm throat, so it is not comparable to the throat figures on other pages.
Warranty: Bernina's 20/5/2 terms come from its general warranty page that does not name the L 850; one dealer adds its own 1 year service warranty.
Price: $3,999 MSRP on Bernina's page against $2,499 that one PatternReview owner paid on a dealer promotion.

ownerThemes.theme: An owner who replaced a 20-year-old Bernina 800DL calls the L 850 substantial and steady at top speed, bought it at $2,499 on promotion, and could not justify the $1,500 step to the L 860.

One unit arrived with a misaligned needle so the 4-thread stitch would not form until adjusted; the same owner notes a chirp alert when the knee lift and pedal are used together, and traced a tension problem to lifting the foot mid-seam.
Buyers cross-shopping the L 850 against the Baby Lock Acclaim weigh Bernina's set-once tension against Baby Lock's continuous automatic tension.

editorial.verdict: A dealer-only 2/3/4 thread air-threading serger at a $3,999 MSRP that buys mechanical refinement, not a touch screen or coverstitch.
editorial.whoFor: A garment sewer who serges often, wants one-step air threading, a knee lifter and Bernina dealer support, and will ask the dealer for a written price.
editorial.skipIf: You want coverstitch in the same machine (L 890), a touch screen (L 860), or a lower price: the Juki MO-1000 also air threads at 1,500 spm for well under half the Bernina MSRP.

strengths: One-step air threading of both loopers from the foot control, plus a built-in needle threader.
Differential feed adjustable while sewing across 0.7 to 2, with a knee lifter and 6-step presser foot pressure.
5 5/8 in of space right of the needle and 3 3/8 in of work height, the same as the L 860 and L 890 and far above the L 460's 2 in.
weaknesses: $3,999 MSRP is double the L 460 and gives up the L 860's touch screen and the L 890's coverstitch; the Juki MO-1000 is the cheaper air-threading rival.
No coverstitch or chainstitch; the thread cutter is a manual chain cutter, not an automatic trimmer.

faqs.q: How much does the Bernina L 850 cost?
faqs.a: Bernina's US page lists a manufacturer suggested retail price of $3,999 (seen 2026-10-02). Bernina is a dealer-only brand, so the price at the counter is set by the dealer. One PatternReview owner reports paying $2,499 on a dealer promotion, an owner figure [verify].

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Bernina L 850 and the L 860?
faqs.a: Per Bernina's pages, the L 860 adds a 4.3 in color touch screen with guided mode, weighs 28.9 lb against 27.1 lb, and lists at a $4,999 MSRP. Stitch count (18), speed (1,500 spm) and the 5 5/8 in of space right of the needle match the L 850.

faqs.q: Does the Bernina L 850 do coverstitch?
faqs.a: No. Bernina's flyer lists 18 overlock, flatlock and rolled hem stitches on 2, 3 and 4 threads, with no coverstitch or chainstitch. Coverstitch is on the L 890, Bernina's overlock and coverstitch combo, which lists 27 stitches, 1,350 spm and an $8,749 MSRP.

faqs.q: Does the Bernina L 850 have air threading?
faqs.a: Yes. Bernina's One-Step Air Threader threads both loopers from the foot control, and there is a built-in needle threader. Owners in our read like the built-in needle threader and the pedal control for needle up and down, and one expert-level owner was very happy with it after nine months. One owner suspects the thread tubes behind a wooly nylon problem.

faqs.q: What needles does the Bernina L 850 use?
faqs.a: ELx705 CF in sizes 70 to 90 (10 to 14), and the standard set is 3 x size 80 and 2 x size 90. Bernina's manual also permits 130/705 H needles if required, while one dealer listing names only the ELx705 sizes.

faqs.q: How heavy is the Bernina L 850?
faqs.a: Bernina's manual gives 27.1 lb (12.3 kg), with a boxed weight of about 37.5 lb (17 kg). The machine measures 16.9 x 11.0 x 13.8 in without the thread stand. A dealer listing gave 18 x 13 x 16 in, which does not match the manual.

faqs.q: Does the Bernina L 850 have a free arm?
faqs.a: Yes. Bernina lists a free arm with a slide-on extension table. Bernina quotes 5 5/8 in of space to the right of the needle, which is not a needle-to-arm throat figure.

faqs.q: What is the warranty on the Bernina L 850?
faqs.a: Bernina's general limited warranty gives 2 years on electrical parts, 5 years on printed circuit boards and 20 years on mechanical parts. It covers parts only, not labor or shipping, applies to the original purchaser for private use, and does not name the L 850. Ask the dealer for the terms in writing [verify].
